method.title: Methodology and sources
method.intro: How the calculator and the comparison work: every formula, every data source, and the limits of what we can estimate.
method.formulas.title: How the calculator works
method.net.title: Greek net pay
method.net.intro: We start from the gross annual salary you enter:
method.net.step1: Employee social contributions (EFKA) = gross pay × the employee contribution rate. They are charged only on pay up to a monthly ceiling.
method.net.step2: Taxable income = gross pay − employee contributions.
method.net.step3: Income tax: taxable income is taxed band by band at the 2026 rates. The rates depend on how many dependent children you have, and lower rates apply up to age 30.
method.net.step4: Tax reduction: a fixed amount, depending on the number of children, is taken off the tax. Above an income threshold it shrinks as income rises.
method.net.step5: Other levies, such as the special solidarity contribution, are added only if they apply to employment income in 2026.
method.net.step6: Annual net pay = gross pay − contributions − final tax − other levies.
method.net.step7: Monthly net pay = annual net ÷ 12. Greek salaries are usually paid in 14 instalments (including the Christmas, Easter and holiday bonuses), so each actual payment is annual net ÷ 14.
method.net.params: The exact rates, bands and thresholds are in the list of tax parameters below, each with its source.
method.fiveCCalc.title: With the Article 5C break
method.fiveCCalc.body: With the break, part of your income is not taxed, so the tax in steps 3–5 is lower. The break lasts a set number of years; after that, the calculator shows your pay without it. That drop is the "cliff" in the timeline chart.
method.fiveCCalc.open: Exactly how the break is applied (to the income or to the tax, and in what order relative to the tax reduction) is still being verified. The calculator follows the rule recorded in the tax parameters.
method.rent.title: Rent in Greece
method.rent.body: Estimated rent = average asking rent in the city (€ per m² per month, from Spitogatos) × the apartment size in m².
method.left.title: Left after rent
method.left.body: Left after rent = monthly net pay − monthly rent, in Greece and in the country where you live now. For your current country we use the net pay and rent you enter; we don't calculate foreign taxes.
method.fx.title: Currency
method.fx.body: Amounts in pounds, dollars or kronor are converted to euros at the latest ECB euro reference rate: amount in EUR = amount ÷ units of that currency per €1.
method.ppp.title: Purchasing power
method.ppp.body: The same euro buys different amounts in different countries. To compare like with like, we express what's left in your current country in Greek prices: amount in Greek prices = amount in EUR × Greek price level ÷ your country's price level. Price levels are OECD price level indices for actual individual consumption.
method.ppp.example: Example: if prices in your country are 40% higher than in Greece, €1,400 left over there is worth about €1,000 in Greek prices.
method.headline.title: The headline percentage
method.headline.body: Difference = (left in Greece − left in your country in Greek prices) ÷ left in your country in Greek prices × 100, rounded to a whole percent. Under 1% either way reads as "about the same". It is worked out separately for the years with the Article 5C break and the years after.
method.peers.title: The comparison page
method.peers.body: Six Eurostat indicators, each for the latest period in which every country shown has a figure. The short sentence above each chart is generated from the data: Greece's gap to the EU-27 average and its rank among the countries shown.
method.fiveC.title: Article 5C: the 50% tax break
method.fiveC.what: If you move your tax residence to Greece and work here, Article 5C of the Greek Income Tax Code exempts {rate} of your income from work from income tax, for {years} years.
method.fiveC.what.generic: If you move your tax residence to Greece and work here, Article 5C of the Greek Income Tax Code exempts 50% of your income from work from income tax, for a limited number of years. The exact rate and duration have not yet been verified against AADE guidance.
method.fiveC.conditions: The main conditions, as the quiz checks them:
method.fiveC.outcomes: The quiz never tells you that you qualify. It gives one of three outcomes: "Likely eligible", "Borderline" or "Likely not eligible". Only AADE decides.
method.fiveC.official: Official guidance: AADE, frequently asked questions on Article 5C (October 2025, in Greek)
method.sources.title: Data sources
method.src.rent: Rent per m² (Athens, Thessaloniki, Heraklion, Patras)
method.src.tax.provider: AADE and legislation (one source per parameter)
method.sources.cadence: Exchange rates are refreshed every working day, OECD and Eurostat data are checked monthly, rents are entered by hand each quarter, and tax rules are checked once a year.
method.sources.licence: Sources: ECB, OECD, Eurostat, Spitogatos. Data are reused under their terms, with attribution.
method.limits.title: Known limitations
method.limit.housing.title: Housing is partly counted twice
method.limit.housing.body: The price level index covers all household consumption, housing included, and we also subtract rent separately. No published index excludes housing for all the countries we cover, so we accept this overlap. It can skew the comparison slightly.
method.limit.asking.title: Asking rents, not signed rents
method.limit.asking.body: Spitogatos figures are averages of advertised prices. The rents people actually sign for are often lower.
method.limit.oneEarner.title: One earner
method.limit.oneEarner.body: We calculate with one person's salary. A second household income isn't included, and we assume you pay the full rent yourself.
method.limit.rules.title: 2026 rules for every year
method.limit.rules.body: The timeline applies the 2026 tax rules to every year. Rates and thresholds will change, but we don't try to guess how. Pay, rents and prices also stay at today's levels.
method.limit.age.title: How age is counted
method.limit.age.body: Lower tax rates apply up to age 30. We work out your age band for each year from your year of birth. The exact rule (the age you reach during the year, or your age on 1 January) is still being verified; where the two rules give different results, we say so.
method.limit.remote.title: Remote work is a grey area
method.limit.remote.body: If you'd work remotely for a foreign company with no presence in Greece, it isn't clear whether Article 5C applies. The quiz marks this as borderline. Get confirmation from a Greek tax adviser before relying on the 50% break.
privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: In short: nothing you enter is stored or sent anywhere, and the site uses no cookies.
privacy.inputs.title: What you enter in the calculator
privacy.inputs.body: Your quiz answers and the figures you enter are processed in your browser, on your device. They are not sent to us or to anyone else, and they are not saved: close or reload the page and they're gone.
privacy.cookies.title: Cookies
privacy.cookies.body: The site sets no cookies and stores nothing on your device. That's why there's no cookie banner.
privacy.analytics.title: Visitor statistics
privacy.analytics.body: We count visits with {provider}. It uses no cookies and never sees what you enter in the calculator.
privacy.analytics.none: We don't use any visitor statistics tool.
privacy.hosting.title: Hosting
privacy.hosting.body: The pages are served by Cloudflare. Like any web host, it processes your IP address to deliver the pages and to protect the site from abuse. We don't keep any logs.
about.title: About
about.name: Nostos (νόστος) is Greek for homecoming.
about.who.title: Who makes it
about.who.body: Nostos is an independent project. It isn't affiliated with any public body, company or tax adviser.
about.why.title: Why
about.why.body: Many people who left Greece during the crisis years, and many who have never lived here, are thinking about moving. The numbers they need are scattered across tax law, statistics and listings. Nostos brings them together, with their sources, so you can judge for yourself.
about.disclaimer.title: Not tax advice
about.disclaimer.body1: Everything here is an estimate based on published figures and the rules as we understand them. Tax rules change, and individual circumstances differ.
about.disclaimer.body2: Nothing on this site is tax, legal or financial advice. Only AADE decides whether you qualify for Article 5C. Confirm with a Greek tax adviser before making decisions.
